test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 25 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A man loses 28% by selling an article for ₹144. If he sells it for ₹288, what will be his gain/loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling price ₹144 corresponds to a 28% loss, which means it is 72% of CP.

The equivalent percentage for ₹288 = (72 / 144) × 288 = 144% of CP.

Since the equivalent value is greater than 100%, there is a profit.

Gain percentage = 144% − 100% = 44%.

**∴ The correct answer is Gain, 44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss percentage = 28%

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹144

New Selling Price (SP₂) = ₹288

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) / (100 − Loss%)

Gain% = (Gain / CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61fd6cfff719ac5dc597005cd0aed1004e20db2a139abbf7c3a0a5d40132ccfe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (144 × 100) / (100 − 28)

⇒ CP = 14400 / 72 = ₹200

⇒ New SP = ₹288

⇒ Gain = New SP − CP = 288 − 200 = ₹88

⇒ Gain% = (88 / 200) × 100 = 44%

**∴ The correct answer is Gain, 44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Final selling price is SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: (a + b − (a × b) / 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

A dealer who claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight makes a profit %. The formula is: Profit % = (Error / (True Value − Error)) × 100.
